old_problem: Procedure and Criteria were TBD, so historical review could not distinguish physical-display firmware enablement from OS monitor state, NVML connection telemetry, Windows WDDM/TCC or vGPU policy. DeepSeek's generic nvidia-smi/GUI suggestion supplied no supported board state, write scope, activation or visual oracle. A false PASS could arise from a connected monitor driven by another GPU, and an unscoped real mode update could rewrite all eligible boards and require recovery after reboot.
disposition_reason: Resolve Engineering Decision Pending and BLOCKED. NVIDIA's Display Mode Selector guide defines the standard Display enabled state as `physical_display_enabled_256MB_bar1`, used for workstation deployments with physically attached displays. The adjacent independent rows map the other two vendor states—display disabled and enabled 8GB scalable mode—confirming this row's intended distinction without merging coverage. NVIDIA also defines supported GPUs, driver-family compatibility, single-adapter syntax, firmware risk, reboot activation and the Windows requirement that WDDM is needed for GPU-accelerated physical output. Exact board/OEM support, OS-specific driver/session configuration, monitor path, pinned tool, verify-existing versus transition branch, final state and recovery are project/runtime gates. Real display pixels plus board mode/BAR1 evidence are required; generic nvidia-smi telemetry is not enough.
decision_basis: The exact XLSX row 1779, same-row DeepSeek/test-json content, GPT V2, historical V3.1 blocked record, original pending/blocked analyses, exact-code search, adjacent rows 1777/1778 and ED rules were read. The actual next formal queue identity was directly opened as Functionality row 1780 / Wistron-HW-00413-V002 / 4362fd0ccbf1d4c0.

NVIDIA defines Physical Display Ports Enabled with 256MB BAR1 for standard workstation deployments with attached physical displays. The exact selector target is `physical_display_enabled_256MB_bar1`; it is not OS screen power, monitor connection telemetry or the separate 8GB scalable mode.

NVIDIA lists RTX A5000/A5500/A6000, RTX 5000/5880/6000 Ada families with 256MB-BAR1 physical-display-enabled factory default, while A40/L20/L40/L40S default disabled. Thus an as-found enabled check and a transition test must be labeled separately and evaluated against the target model's documented default/project recipe.

The tool syntax is `displaymodeselector --gpumode physical_display_enabled_256MB_bar1 -i <index>`; omitting `-i` may switch all eligible adapters. Serial/UUID/BDF-to-index binding is mandatory immediately before a scoped update.

The selector updates board firmware and requires reboot. On Windows, NVIDIA distinguishes TCC from WDDM and states that enabled ports in TCC may show a picture without GPU-accelerated graphics; WDDM and a post-reboot accelerated rendering check are therefore part of Windows acceptance.

Machine state and pixels are independent evidence: active 256MB BAR1/mode does not prove the correct connector/monitor/session works, while a lit display can be driven by another GPU. Correlate EDID/connector/render workload to the exact BDF and capture genuine visual evidence under ED-08/ED-20.
The separate 8GB scalable row retains its own workload/visual contract; this row validates standard 256MB-BAR1 physical output and must not claim scalable-visualization coverage.
No Display Mode Selector command, GPU firmware update, driver-mode change, reboot, display action, log clear or other DUT action was executed.

test_case.test_name: NVIDIA Display Enabled Mode — physical display enabled with 256MB BAR1
test_case.purpose: For one exact supported and OEM-qualified NVIDIA GPU, verify or transition to `physical_display_enabled_256MB_bar1`, activate the state through the required reboot, prove the correct physical connector produces stable GPU-accelerated output on the approved OS/driver session, and leave or restore the signed final configuration without altering other adapters.
required_package: Exact SUT and supported GPU model/SKU/serial/UUID/PCI BDF plus verified Display Mode Selector index, VBIOS and documented factory/current mode
OEM/vGPU-certified system approval for 256MB-BAR1 physical-display mode and project choice of as-found verification versus state transition plus signed final mode

NVIDIA-authorized hash/version-pinned Display Mode Selector and compatible RTX Enterprise or Data Center driver; on Windows, approved WDDM/TCC state and exact target GPU driver-mode command if change is required
Exact GPU connector/cable/display/EDID/resolution/refresh and OS session map, independent non-target console/BMC/SSH path and a deterministic accelerated rendering/display pattern with visual oracle
Maintenance, graphics/compute/vGPU workload drain, stable power, immediate firmware/driver-mode/reboot approvals, signed prior-mode recovery artifact and vendor/OEM board-service path
test_case.test_command: NOT STARTED; firmware/driver-mode/reboot approval required for transition. Bind serial/UUID/BDF to one tool index, verify board/VBIOS/OEM/tool/driver support, and preserve mode, BAR1, PCIe/GPU/driver mode, sessions, connector/EDID, rendering path and OS/BMC events. If the owner selected verify-existing and the board is already in the target state, do not rewrite firmware; validate active `physical_display_enabled_256MB_bar1`, 256MB BAR1 and the exact accelerated display path. Otherwise drain users, obtain immediate approval and run the pinned selector once for only that adapter: `displaymodeselector --gpumode physical_display_enabled_256MB_bar1 -i <VERIFIED_INDEX>`. Apply any separately approved OS driver mode required by NVIDIA (Windows WDDM for accelerated output), then perform the required approved reboot. Verify active mode/BAR1, same GPU/PCIe/driver identity, EDID/connector ownership and real GPU-accelerated visual output; restore only per the signed final-state plan. Never omit `-i`, treat a lit but non-accelerated TCC picture as PASS, clear logs or retry automatically.
test_case.expected_result: Exactly the selected supported GPU is or becomes active in `physical_display_enabled_256MB_bar1` with the vendor-defined 256MB BAR1 after the required approved activation, and no other adapter changes. The exact connector/EDID/display is driven by that GPU at the approved resolution/refresh; the deterministic pattern renders without blanking, corruption, edge loss or instability and, on Windows, is NVIDIA GPU-accelerated under the approved WDDM state rather than a non-accelerated TCC picture. GPU/VBIOS, PCIe link, driver, sessions, host services and events remain healthy and the signed final mode is proven.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires authoritative model/OEM/tool/driver applicability, exact one-GPU identity, active 256MB-BAR1 firmware mode, unchanged non-target GPUs, connector/EDID ownership, actual timestamped accelerated visual evidence, complete reboot/health and final-state proof. A selector exit, nvidia-smi Display Active, BAR1 alone, a lit monitor from another GPU or non-accelerated TCC output does not PASS. Unsupported hardware is N/A only with authoritative applicability evidence; absent qualification/recovery is BLOCKED. Wrong/all-GPU update, mode/BAR1/driver mismatch, blank/corrupt/unstable output, missing acceleration, GPU/PCIe/driver/event regression or failed restore is reported for engineer FAIL/BLOCKED disposition. The end user decides the verdict.
safety_gate: Require exact supported model/VBIOS, OEM-qualified platform, pinned selector/driver and OS-specific session plan; do not generalize this mode or change a production/sole-console GPU without independent access.
Re-bind serial/UUID/BDF to the selector index immediately before action and always use `-i <VERIFIED_INDEX>`; never permit the tool's all-adapter default scope.

Treat firmware mode, Windows driver-mode and reboot as distinct state changes with separate immediate approvals, stable power, drained workloads/sessions, full output and pre-approved restoration/recovery.
Require both active mode/BAR1 and real connector-bound accelerated visual evidence; a connected monitor or successful request cannot substitute for pixels and GPU ownership.
Stop on identity, compatibility, write, reboot, driver, PCIe, BAR1, output, session or evidence anomaly. Do not retry, switch modes, reset, reboot or power-cycle automatically.
expected_evidence: Source Key/Variant, branch (verify-existing or transition), model factory/current/target reference, OEM approval, SUT/GPU serial/UUID/BDF/index and selector/VBIOS/driver hashes/versions
Pre-state firmware mode/BAR1, PCIe/GPU/driver-mode/sessions, connector/cable/display/EDID/resolution and rendering-path identity, preserved events and recovery readiness
For transition: exact scoped selector and any separately approved driver-mode command with full outputs, approvals and no-retry/no-other-adapter audit
Reboot/OS-ready timeline; post active 256MB-BAR1 mode, WDDM/driver and same-GPU health; timestamped connector-bound accelerated pattern visual evidence
Final state or approved restore, complete GPU/PCIe/OS/BMC events, recovery actions and engineer-owned PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED/N/A verdict
test_case.recovery: On wrong identity, unsupported combination, selector/driver-mode error, incomplete update, reboot failure, missing GPU, mode/BAR1 mismatch, non-accelerated or lost/corrupt output, stop and preserve tool, VBIOS, driver, console and event state. Do not rerun or choose another mode. Use independent BMC/SSH/non-target display and the owner/OEM-approved signed prior-mode/driver recovery or board-service procedure; any restoration and reboot are separately approved and fully evidenced.
